resolutions: Passive voice consumes an owner-authorized active VNC Source and cannot be authorized by a copied passive formula or surface form.
The user requests passive voice; object promotion, case relocation, subject deletion, and nonactive-stem use are grammatical consequences rather than separate choices.
A passive Source must contain a specific projective object or a specific reflexive object; an intransitive or nonspecific-only Source is rejected.
An active Source subject is removed completely from the passive Result and can never survive as a Nahuatl agent phrase.
An English passive that names its agent must therefore be composed as an active Nahuatl clause rather than by adding an agent control.
The passive stem comes from the owner-issued Lesson 20 nonactive record and cannot be typed independently.
A nonspecific-only or intransitive Source belongs to the Lesson 22 impersonal route and is never silently converted from a failed passive request.
With one specific projective object, the Result uses the intransitive VNC formula after that object becomes the passive subject.
The promoted object's person and number relocate from objective positions into the nominative subject positions without another user decision.
Different active subjects can therefore collapse into the same passive Result because none of their subject information survives.
A third-person plural animate object remains third-person plural when promoted to passive subject.
A grammatically present silent third-person singular or common object promotes exactly like a sounded object and does not require a second visibility choice.
Silence is a typed realization of the object relation, not evidence that the active Source is intransitive.
A single reflexive object's participant is already fixed by the active Source subject, so promotion does not expose a new person choice.
After reflexive-object promotion, shuntline ne remains automatically as the reflexive relation and makes the passive Result transitive.
Retained ne is not a second participant and cannot be independently added, removed, or reassigned.
Reflexive versus reciprocal remains a genuine Source interpretation choice only for a plural participant where both readings are licensed.
With one reflexive and one specific projective object, the projective object is the only eligible passive subject and no promotion-target choice remains.
The reflexive object in that mixed Source converts automatically to shuntline ne after the projective object promotes.
The resulting ne continues the original reflexive relation and never introduces a new participant.
With two specific projective objects, Source-authorized mainline status determines which object promotes.
The shuntline specific object remains in the passive Result instead of being discarded with the active subject.
A silently realized shuntline object remains grammatically present and its singular or common-number ambiguity is preserved rather than guessed away.
A retained third-person plural animate shuntline object restores its sounded qu-im realization in the passive transform.
The user resolves mainline and shuntline roles only while composing a genuinely ambiguous active Source; the passive operation never asks again.
When a Source has only one specific object, specificity fixes the promotion target regardless of whether that object was mainline or shuntline.
A nonspecific human object remains tē and a nonspecific nonhuman object remains tla after the specific object promotes.
The retained nonspecific object keeps the passive Result transitive without becoming a candidate for promotion.
Alternative participant-role readings remain available where Andrews licenses them, including unlikely readings, but the application does not silently choose one gloss.
A displayed short te in the narrow printed formula environment is a contextual projection of typed tē rather than a change to the object relation.
Three-object passive Sources reuse the same promotion and retention rules; object count does not authorize a separate shortcut or mode.
Among three specific objects, the typed mainline object promotes and every licensed shuntline object remains with its own person, number, and realization.
A three-object Source containing reflexive or nonspecific relations preserves those relations by the same rules used in the two-object cases.
User control remains at active Source composition: once typed object roles exist, passive application cannot reopen or override their promotion hierarchy.
Clicked role cues explain the already authorized promotion and retention history but cannot infer or change Source roles from formula text.
A wish, command or exhortation, or admonition consumes a completed passive VNC instead of rebuilding its voice structure.
The user chooses the ordinary sentence force while passive promotion, retained objects, and the nonactive stem remain automatic.
Passive mood composition reuses the same mood, tense, number, negation, and introductory controls used by active VNCs.
No passive-specific wish, command, exhortation, or admonition control is grammatically authorized.
A reflexively marked VNC with contextual passive meaning remains grammatically active and never enters the passive voice route.
The reflexive object marker remains part of the generated formula when a contextual passive interpretation is selected.
Literal reflexive and contextual passive readings are a genuine interpretation choice only when both are supported, and the choice never changes the finite form.
The subject of this contextual construction is normally nonanimate and is interpreted as patient rather than agent.
An animate subject is licensed only with the patient interpretation documented by the construction, never by reanalyzing it as the performer.
Specific and generic reference remain contextual facts; generic reference does not manufacture a new plural or voice operation.
Unknown or contextually unimportant human agency motivates the passive reading without authorizing a Nahuatl agent phrase.
The listed active-reflexive examples and English glosses guide reading but cannot authorize a copied surface or a new passive morphology route.
